facts.subject: AWS registered lobbying objective
facts.value: Bundestag lobbying register records AWS EMEA objective on EUCS as deletion of sovereignty requirements, because AWS argued they did not strengthen cybersecurity.

facts.subject: Cross-industry demand to reject sovereignty criteria
facts.value: A broad industry statement called on EU member states, EU institutions and ENISA to reject EUCS sovereignty requirements and described them as politically motivated.

facts.subject: US industry escalation through TTC channel
facts.value: CCIA and other US groups sent concerns to the US administration ahead of the EU-US TTC and advocated removal of nationality-based ownership restrictions.

facts.subject: Industry support after draft changed
facts.value: BSA/GDA publicly welcomed the new draft specifically because sovereignty requirements had been removed and urged EU institutions to proceed without reintroducing them.

facts.subject: Draft policy delta
facts.value: Reuters reported that the March 22 2024 EUCS draft removed prior stringent sovereignty requirements and retained transparency about data location, processing and applicable laws.

facts.subject: Compromise contested by opposing industries
facts.value: Reuters reported the Belgian compromise removed prior sovereignty requirements, was welcomed by Big Tech, opposed by European providers, and failed to reach a vote at that meeting.

facts.subject: Government counter-position
facts.value: France, Germany and Italy jointly called for EU cloud certification protecting sensitive data, including against extraterritorial laws.

facts.subject: French position persisted through change period
facts.value: French government said it continued to defend EUCS protection for sensitive data against extraterritorial legislation.

facts.subject: French national certification control
facts.value: France stated that AWS or any provider must meet SecNumCloud 3.2, including protection against extra-European law, to obtain trusted-cloud qualification in France.

facts.subject: EUCS institutional baseline
facts.value: ENISA describes EUCS as voluntary EU-wide cloud certification with basic, substantial and high assurance levels and technical-security harmonisation goals.

facts.subject: Sovereignty later reintroduced through procurement framework
facts.value: Commission states its Cloud Sovereignty Framework uses explicit sovereignty/resilience assurance levels and 48 criteria and is intended as a public-sector benchmark.

facts.subject: Commission applied sovereignty criteria in procurement
facts.value: Commission used its sovereignty framework in a €180m procurement and required at least a data-sovereignty assurance level for eligibility.

facts.subject: EU architecture shifted rather than sovereignty disappearing
facts.value: A 2026 Commission proposal establishes a cloud sovereignty framework and states that work will resume on EUCS, showing the 2024 EUCS removal did not amount to permanent abandonment of sovereignty policy.

facts.subject: European cloud-provider position was not monolithic
facts.value: CISPE backed reaching an EUCS compromise while preserving customer sovereignty choice and special high-sovereignty use cases, complicating a simple Big-Tech-versus-Europe model.

facts.subject: Lobbying-target / policy-delta congruence
facts.value: AWS had an explicit registered objective to delete sovereignty requirements; the March 2024 draft had already removed them. Congruence and chronology are supported; causal attribution is not closed by those facts alone.

facts.subject: Sustained multi-channel industry pressure
facts.value: Industry pressure against sovereignty criteria was repeated across joint statements, direct advocacy to EU actors, and escalation through US-government/TTC channels before and during the draft change.
